cause: KillAllFunctions only marked clean. The next Update first admitted all queued functions, then cleared them, discarding new work scheduled after cancellation. A callback cancelling its own generation still allowed other already-due callbacks to run in the same Update. The current callback also remained in the map while executing, so recursive Update replayed it and cancellation could invalidate its node.
repair: Clear the pending queue under its existing mutex at cancellation; clear cancelled active callbacks before admitting the fresh pending queue. Move and erase the current function before invocation, then stop/clear the old active generation if its callback cancels. Leave freshly scheduled work pending until the next normal update. Existing clock, equal-time order, queue separation, ABI/header/layout and public APIs retained.
example: Existing Sentinax DoAction(1) calls KillAllDelayedEvents then schedules a10s summons cleanup. Old scheduler discards that new callback; native tests exercise the exact cancellation/rearm API sequence without claiming whole Sentinax or artifact traversal.
